children: Consumer prices in Morocco fell by 0.3% year-on-year in August 2026, following a 0.6% decrease in July, as deflation persisted for a second straight month.
Food and non-alcoholic beverages posted a sharper price decline of 4.2% in August, compared with 4.0% in July, while communication prices fell 0.2% for a second month.
Meanwhile, inflation moderated for housing and utilities (1.4% vs 1.5%) and restaurants and hotels (2.3% vs 2.4%).
On the other hand, price growth accelerated sharply for transportation (7.3% vs 4.1%).
The core inflation index, which excludes products with volatile prices and those subject to public tariffs, increased by 0.2% from July and by 0.1% from August 2025.
On a monthly basis, the CPI rose by 0.8%, after a 1% decline in the previous month.

title: Morocco Posts Deflation for 2nd Month
